2. The assertion in the writ petition is that the petitioner (one in number) is owner of lands bearing Block No. 197(2), 252(3), 254 (1), village Hazira, Taluka Choryasi, District Surat, which had been acquired for the purposes of respondent no.4, namely Essar Steel Company Ltd., Hazira, Surat,
under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short as the "Act' 1894") for expansion of the Company.
3. The statement in paragraph '2' of the writ petition is that by receiving application from ESSAR Company for land acquisition on 31.01.2005, the Collector, Surat started the proceedings.

The acquisition notifications dated 03.06.2005 and 16.01.2006 under Sections 4 and 6 of the Act' 1894;
respectively were published.

The contention is that 152 objections were filed by the farmers of Hazira against the said acquisition, hearing was arranged, wherein most of the farmers were absent but the State Government finalised the land acquisition process.
4. The statement in paragraph '3' of the writ petition is that the petitioner's father had three brothers who had inherited the lands in question from their father.
The father of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10944/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined petitioner, thus, was co-owner of 1/3rd of the total area of the aforesaid three plots.
The petitioner also has one brother, so the share of the petitioner is half out of 1/3rd of the property of his father, which comes to 2343 sq. mtrs.

From the statement made in paragraph '3' of the writ petition, it is pertinent to note that apart from the petitioner, there are other co-owners of the lands in question but none of them are impleaded herein.

5. The further assertion in the Writ petition is that the Company did not pay the award amount and compensation in the year 2014 and has not taken the physical possession of the property and as such the petitioner approached the Land Acquisition and Compensation Management Officer of the Company, viz. Arcelor Mittal Nippon Steel India Ltd., Administrative Officer, Hazira, Surat.

sentences.text: 6. The further contention in the Writ petition is that the award was passed without consulting the land owners and it does not reflect the real market value of the property at the time of acquisition.
The physical possession of the land and the house was with the petitioner till 17.01.2024.
The contention in paragraph '7' of the writ petition is that the Company did not pay compensation and the award was for open land of the petitioner herein, which is a different survey number.

The further statement in the same paragraph is that the petitioner visited the company, met the land acquisition officer, viz. respondent no.5 and had discussion for the due NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10944/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined amount or rest of the amount of compensation under the award, but the respondent no.5 has not responded properly.

7. It is, thus, sought to be submitted by the petitioner that the Company neither paid compensation satisfactorily prior to the year 2014 nor possession of the lands in question was taken and, as such,
by virtue of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short as the "Act' 2013"), entire land acquisition proceedings would lapse.

sentences.text: In various paragraphs of the Writ petition, the petitioner seeks to submit that the physical possession of the lands in question has not been taken prior to the promulgation of the Act' 2013 and, as such, the land acquisition proceedings cannot be said to have been brought to its logical end.

8. Taking note of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the averments made in the Writ petition, suffice it to note that interpretation of the provisions of Section 24(2) has been made by the Apex Court in the case of Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal [(2020) 8 SCC 129], which is extracted hereinunder :-.
"366.3.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal [(2020) 8 SCC 129]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The word "or" used in Section 24(2) between possession and compensation has to be read as "nor" or as "and".

The deemed lapse of land acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act takes place where due to inaction of authorities for five years or more prior to commencement of the said Act, the possession of land has not been taken nor compensation has been paid.
In other words, in case possession has been taken, compensation has not been paid then there is no lapse.
Similarly, if compensation has been paid, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10944/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined possession has not been taken then there is no lapse.
The expression "paid" in the main part of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act does not include a deposit of compensation in court.
The consequence of non-deposit is provided in the proviso to Section 24(2)

in case it has not been deposited with respect to majority of landholdings then all beneficiaries (landowners) as on the date of notification for land acquisition under Section 4 of the 1894 Act shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of the 2013 Act.
In case the obligation under Section 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has not been fulfilled

,
interest under Section 34 of the said Act can be granted.

sentences.text: 3 compensation (in court) does not result in the lapse of land acquisition proceedings.

In case of non-deposit with respect to the majority of holdings for five years or more,
compensation under the 2013 Act has to be paid to the "landowners" as on the date of notification for land acquisition under Section 4 of the 1894 Act.

In case a person has been tendered the compensation as provided under Section 31(1) of the 1894 Act, it is not open to him to claim that acquisition has lapsed under Section 24(2) due to non-payment or non-deposit of compensation in court.
The obligation to pay is complete by tendering the amount under Section 31(1).
The landowners who had refused to accept compensation or who sought reference for higher compensation, cannot claim that the acquisition proceedings had lapsed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.
The proviso to Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act is to be treated as part of Section 24(2), not part of Section 24(1)(b).
The mode of taking possession under the 1894 Act and as contemplated under Section 24(2) is by drawing of inquest report/memorandum.

Once award has been passed on taking possession under Section 16 NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10944/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined of the 1894 Act, the land vests in State there is no divesting provided under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act,
as once possession has been taken there is no lapse under Section 24(2).

The provisions of Section 24(2) providing for a deemed lapse of proceedings are applicable in case authorities have failed due to their inaction to take possession and pay compensation for five years or more before the 2013 Act came into force, in a proceeding for land acquisition pending with the authority concerned as on 1-1-2014.
The period of subsistence of interim orders passed by court has to be excluded in the computation of five years.
Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act does not give rise to new cause of action to question the legality of concluded proceedings of land acquisition.
Section 24 applies to a proceeding pending on the date of enforcement of the 2013 Act i.e. 1-1-2014.

It does not revive stale and time- barred claims and does not reopen concluded proceedings nor allow landowners to question the legality of mode of taking possession to reopen proceedings or mode of deposit of compensation in the treasury instead of court to invalidate acquisition."
9. Having noticed the above, we may record that sub- section (2) of Section 24 talks of a situation where neither the award has been made nor physical possession of the land has been taken.

It is clarified by the Apex Court in Indore Development Authority (supra) that words "physical possession" occurring in sub-section (2) of Section 24 has to be understood and mean as the paper possession of the acquired land as well, which is an approved mode of transfer of possession under the Old Act' 1894.

sentences.text: Moreover, the submission made by the learned counsel NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10944/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined for the petitioner that the physical possession of the lands in question was with the petitioner and it was taken in the year 2024 itself is a bald statement not supported by any material on record.
As per own admission of the petitioner in the Writ petition, the compensation has been paid to the petitioner in the year 2014.

We do not find any reason to believe that the Company paid compensation directly to the petitioner, inasmuch as,
as per the requirement of the Act' 1894, the compensation was required to be deposited in the office of the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

It is an admitted fact of the matter that award was declared in the year 2008, much prior to the promulgation of the Act' 2013 and, thus, the acquisition proceedings under the old Act' 1894 had been culminated much earlier.
The contention of the petitioner that full and satisfactory award amount has not been paid to the petitioner is neither here nor there.
11. We may also record that in view of the own admission of the petitioner that there are other co-owners of the lands in question and the fact is that none of them have been joined.

As per own case of the petitioner, the lands in question is inherited by the petitioner from his father who had other two brothers who jointly owned the lands in question, but there is complete silence in the Writ petition whether the petitioner's father is alive or not.
We find that the present petition has been filed with incorrect and incomplete facts.
12. The Writ petition is accordingly dismissed.

However, for any issue with regard to disbursement of full amount of compensation determined under the Award passed in the year NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10944/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 2008, it is kept open to the petitioner to lay his claim before the Land Acquisition Officer, who shall deal with the same keeping in mind that there are other co-owners of the lands in question.
